newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits rise 3.5 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits rise 3.5 pct in November.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in November rose 3.5 percent to C$2.20 billion, seasonally adjusted, from October, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Oct Month pct chg Yr pct change
Statistics Canada said the increase in building permits was in line with low mortgage interest rates and a stronger demand for new and existing homes.

"The latest figures are encouraging signs for the housing sector, as mortgage rates in November reached their lowest level in a generation and resale activity set a new monthly record," the agency said.
It said applications for non-residential building permits declined for the fourth consecutive month to their second lowest level in 1996.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labour and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
